card.band: 4 h. Multi-dimensional scoring gives several levers. Frontier agents beat best-fit in some trials. The weaker model matches the baseline.
card.cheat: Hidden streams use different parameters and seeds. A policy memorising item sequences cannot transfer.
card.grading: Percent excess bins over the lower bound on hidden streams drawn from other shapes, scales, lengths up to 100k, and dimensions. Normalised between the baseline and our reference.
card.reference: Our tuned policy with lookahead and a repacking-free heuristic, measured. The known FunSearch results are only scalar and give context only.
card.source: https://github.com/google-deepmind/funsearch/tree/main/bin_packing, Apache-2.0; instances regenerated synthetically (OR-Library has no stated licence)
card.task: /app ships an online bin packing simulator generalised to 2-D and 3-D vector items, a best-fit baseline and a generator for Weibull and triplet-style streams. The agent designs and trains a placement policy, which may include lookahead and learned scoring, on shipped distributions.
card.title: Online vector bin packing policy with a distribution split

source_notes: Notebook q:"Data from the OR3 benchmark, containing 20 bin packing instances each with 500 items." Weibull 5k: 5 instances x 5,000 items, capacity 100; OR3 capacity 150. OOD split: tune on Weibull-like or OR1-OR2 style, hidden on different Weibull shape/scale, n=10k-100k, or triplet class (binpack5-8, cap 100). Weakness: single lever (one priority function), tiny eval; to make multi-lever extend to vector/2D bin packing or add offline repacking + lookahead. INFERRED: ~2-10 s per eval (pure-Python loop over items with numpy over bins). Notes: FunSearch paper (nature.com) paywalled/redirected, not opened. Overlap: well-known public task.
source_version: Baseline: best-fit priority function (skeleton `return -(bins - item)`) in bin_packing.ipynb; evaluate() returns negative mean number of bins. -> Reference: FunSearch-discovered priority functions from the same notebook. Printed results: OR3 best fit 212.0 bins (5.37% over L1 bound 201.2) -> FunSearch 207.45 (3.11%); Weibull 5k best fit 2067.0 (3.98%) -> 2001.4 (0.68%).

facts.claim: google-deepmind/funsearch repo has a bin_packing directory containing bin_packing.ipynb (the only file listed), at the pinned head cc53f27
Repository licence is Apache-2.0 (as reported by the GitHub API in source_facts); the directory page itself shows no licence text, so this was not re-verified on the page
OR-Library bin packing instances (binpack1-8, Falkenauer): uniform class u1-4 sizes in (20,100) with bin 150; triplet class t5-8 with bin 100, n/3 optimum
OR-Library bin packing page states no licence or redistribution terms, so the seed's choice to regenerate instances synthetically is needed

FunSearch Weibull setup: 5 instances x 5,000 items, Weibull shape 3 scale 45, capacity 100, lb/n averaged over the five instances; evolved heuristic c14 (secondary account, original Nature paper not opened)
Original FunSearch Nature paper text was opened and checked for its bin packing results
A standard public benchmark exists for online vector (multi-dimensional) bin packing with lookahead and learned placement across 2-D and 3-D items
Lookahead placement for online 3-D bin packing with MCTS exists in the literature (N=4 known upcoming parcels), so lookahead itself is not novel
Later papers reuse the FunSearch Weibull(3,45) five-instance setup as a benchmark

full_card.band: Expected 4-5 h frontier work for a strong policy; a frontier agent should beat best-fit on OOD streams in some trials but not reach the tuned reference on average; weaker model stalls near best-fit. No dated public evidence.
full_card.build_cost: About 3 days: simulator with vector/3-D items, generator, baseline, reference policy, grader and tests.
full_card.deliverable: A placement policy (scoring/lookahead) that outputs bin choice per item, scored as percent excess over lower bound on hidden OOD streams up to 100k items.
full_card.gates_anticheat: Hidden streams use unseen seeds and parameters from the shipped generator; grader fixed and sealed; agent cannot edit grader; policy must be deterministic on fixed seeds; reject policies that read stream identity.
full_card.grading_surface: Executable oracle with unlimited generator over shape, scale, length and dimension; thousands of possible streams, scored by code.
full_card.local_fit: Pure Python plus numpy, CPU only, fits 8 cores and 16 GB; eval of 100k items in pure Python is unmeasured and may take minutes.
full_card.lookup: partial: 1-D FunSearch priority function c14 and notebook are public; vector/2-D/3-D lookahead variant not found as a public solution.
full_card.provenance: DeepMind FunSearch repo bin_packing notebook (Apache-2.0 per API, pinned head cc53f27, pushed 2024-02-05); FunSearch Weibull(3,45) setup via secondary sources; OR-Library instances used only for regenerated analogues.
full_card.reference: Seed author's tuned lookahead policy, claimed measured but no artifact seen; FunSearch c14 is a public 1-D priority function only.
full_card.ships: Online 1-D bin packing simulator extended to 2-D/3-D vector items, best-fit baseline, Weibull and triplet stream generator, distribution split (tune vs hidden OOD). Not yet built.
full_card.similarity: l0 neighbour S-rs-023 at 0.207 (above 0.15, needs a check of its subject); FunSearch 1-D Weibull benchmark is public and reused in several papers, so the base task is crowded.

Band.why: No dated public evidence; frontier likely earns partial credit, and the brief's band claims are internal, so at most 3.

Build.why: About 3 days to build simulator, generator, baseline, reference and grader.

Fit.why: CPU-only Python with numpy fits the sandbox; 100k-item eval runtime is the open question.

Hor.why: Core lever is one scoring/placement function; 4 h tier is ample for a strong agent to reach a good policy quickly.

Lic.why: Apache-2.0 per API; OR-Library has no licence, so instances are regenerated and that is handled.

Multi.why: Several distribution buckets and dimensions give partial credit, but most levers collapse into one scoring function.

Nov.why: The 1-D Weibull FunSearch benchmark is a public task with the same deliverable; only the vector extension differs, and l0 neighbour is 0.207.

Real.why: Real Apache-2.0 repo and real FunSearch Weibull setup, but the 2-D/3-D vector extension is not a real subject.

Ref.why: Reference is an unbuilt tuned policy; no artifact to measure, and FunSearch c14 covers only 1-D.

Seal.why: Reference and hidden seeds can stay out of reach; the 1-D FunSearch priority function is public, so a recall path exists.

Surf.why: Generator-based streams give an effectively unlimited executable oracle over shape, scale, length and dimension.

spike_plan.kill_if: Best-fit is within 0.5 points of the best of ten tuned candidates on all OOD buckets (no headroom), or a 100k-item eval exceeds 10 minutes, or results are non-deterministic.
spike_plan.pass_if: Some non-trivial policy beats best-fit by at least 2 percentage points on OOD streams and one 100k-item eval takes under 60 s.
steps: Clone google-deepmind/funsearch at cc53f27 into a throwaway container; read bin_packing.ipynb and extract the priority function and Weibull generator.
Write a 1-D online simulator: best-fit and first-fit baselines plus the FunSearch priority; generate Weibull(3,45) 5 x 5,000 items at capacity 100; lb = ceil(sum/cap); report percent excess.
Time one 100k-item stream in pure Python with numpy over bins; record seconds per eval.
Generate OOD streams (different shape and scale, plus triplet cap 100) and check whether a simple lookahead or learned scoring beats best-fit by at least 2 points on at least 2 buckets.
Run the same seed twice and confirm identical bin counts (determinism).

v1.summary: The 1-D FunSearch Weibull bin packing setup is real, Apache-2.0 and public, but the base is crowded and the seed's actual novelty lies in the unbuilt 2-D/3-D vector extension and its reference. It is not killed; it passes conditionally on a spike showing best-fit leaves measurable headroom on OOD streams and 100k-item evals run in reasonable time.
